In acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (p.1175), abciximab has been used as an adjunct to primary PCI, including coronary stenting, and has been shown to reduce reinfarction rates and mortality,16 with benefit persisting long-term.17 There is some evidence that starting treatment as soon as possible rather than immediately before the procedure may provide additional bene- fit.18,19 Abciximab has also been used as an adjunct to thrombol- ysis and some benefit has been shown,20 but this appears to be offset by an increased bleeding rate, even when reduced doses of thrombolytics are used.21,22 In patients with unstable angina (p.1157) receiving noninterventional treatment, a large study23 with abciximab failed to show any benefit over placebo, al- though other glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors have a role in such patients. Some promising results have been reported with intracoronary abciximab in patients with acute coronary syndromes,24 and with abciximab-coated stents in patients with acute myocardial infarc- tion.25 1.
